_meta: Machinevertaling (nl naar en) van de eigen factcheck brandweerman-frankrijk van Factiz, eigen werk van de redactie (B82, B84), door claude-sonnet-5-5, eigenvertaling-v1; doublecheck/eigenvertaling.py, PLAN #37.8.

velden.kop: Firefighter in Bordeaux injured by an exploding aerosol can, not by young people with petrol
velden.oordeel_zin: A firefighter was briefly hit by a jet of flame on 29 September when an aerosol can exploded in a barricade fire; nobody doused him with petrol or set him alight [1] [3].
velden.bewering: Youths doused a firefighter with petrol during the protests in France and set him on fire.
velden.kort: On 1 and 2 October, Dutch-language posts circulated on X saying that young people in France doused a firefighter with petrol and set him on fire [8]. On 29 September in Bordeaux, a firefighter was indeed briefly hit by a jet of flame when an aerosol can exploded in a barricade fire he was trying to put out [1] [3]. Petrol had nothing to do with it; on 1 October in Marseille, it was a headteacher who was doused with petrol [5] [6].
velden.tekst:
On Thursday 1 October at 21:12, a Dutch-language post appeared on X: young people were said to have doused a firefighter with petrol and set him on fire during the protests in France [8]. A second post, the afternoon after, placed it in Bordeaux [8]. On 2 October an English-language account shared a photo with the same story, which according to CORRECTIV was viewed seven million times and was responded to by Elon Musk [11].

What really happened is set out in the French press: on Tuesday 29 September at around 12:30, school pupils blocked the lycée Montaigne in the rue Sainte-Catherine in Bordeaux, and a barricade was burning in the street at one entrance [1]. A firefighter walked up to the fire to put it out, and at that moment something in the fire exploded: a jet of flame briefly engulfed him [1] [2].

According to the prefecture of the Gironde, it was an aerosol can that was lying in the fire [3]. The firefighter was lightly injured, went to hospital and was back at the fire station the same afternoon [1]. The prefect said he will be unable to work for a few days [1]. In videos from BFMTV and Le Figaro, shot from two angles, nobody sets him alight and after the jet of flame he walks back a few metres himself [4] [11] [12].

Petrol does not appear in any of the reports about Bordeaux [1] [3]. The public prosecutor's office in Bordeaux did open an investigation into deliberate arson causing serious injury; whether the aerosol can was put in the fire on purpose was for that investigation to establish [1].

Something did happen with petrol that week, but in Marseille and not to a firefighter: on Thursday 1 October, the headteacher was doused with petrol at the lycée Victor-Hugo there, and according to the prosecutor's office he was injured [5] [6]. According to another account, the petrol splashed onto teachers when a pupil wanted to throw it into a rubbish bin [7]. At the lycée Saint-Exupéry the same morning, hundreds of young people surrounded a fire engine, chased the firefighters away and set the vehicle on fire [5] [7]. None of those reports mentions a firefighter being set alight [5] [6] [7].

Fact-checkers in other languages reached the same result: An-Nahar on 5 October, EFE Verifica on 6 October, CORRECTIV on 12 October and ZDFheute on 14 October [9] [10] [11] [12]. According to CORRECTIV, the photo is real; the photographer confirmed this to AFP [11]. In Dutch, Knack wrote a fact-check, which was online by 19 October at the latest [13].
velden.niet_weten: We do not know which image appears in the Dutch-language posts. CORRECTIV calls the photo real, while An-Nahar saw an image that differs from the videos and may have been staged [9] [11]. Perhaps two images were circulating. We also do not know whether anyone deliberately put the spray can in the fire, or what the public prosecutor's investigation produced.
nog_uitzoeken: Which image the two Dutch-language posts showed: the real photo by Guillaume Bonnaud, a staged version or a video. The posts are gone.
Whether the Bordeaux public prosecutor's office released anything about the investigation, and whether anyone deliberately put the spray can in the fire.
Other fact-checkers differ in their verdicts: ZDFheute and Mimikama chose misleading, CORRECTIV, EFE Verifica and An-Nahar chose false. We chose false.
tijdlijn: A firefighter is hit by a jet of flame at a barricade in front of the lycée Montaigne in Bordeaux [1].
BFMTV posts the video of the moment on X [4].
In Marseille, a headteacher is doused with petrol and a fire engine is set on fire [5] [6].
The first Dutch-language post: doused with petrol and set on fire [8].
A second Dutch-language post places it in Bordeaux [8].
An-Nahar: the claim is not true [9].
CORRECTIV: the photo is real, nobody set the firefighter alight [11].
By this day at the latest, the Knack fact-check is online [13].
beeld_bijschrift: BFMTV on X, 29 September 2026: the video of the firefighter at the lycée Montaigne in Bordeaux.
beeld_alt: Video by BFMTV: a firefighter walks up to a small fire in the street, the flames shoot up and die down immediately.
